title: Cohomology Adds Structure
notes: Open by naming the shift in purpose. Homology was already powerful because it found holes, but cohomology becomes a structure theory because reversed arrows let classes be pulled back, multiplied, and paired. Keep the source span visible so the audience knows this is the chapter route, not a disconnected algebra detour.

title: From Chains To Cochains
notes: Use the image as the first invariant anchor. A cochain is not a new geometric simplex; it is a tester placed on chains. The formula delta phi equals phi after partial is the whole mechanism: the boundary is applied in chains, then the cochain evaluates. That reversal is why pullback becomes natural.

title: The First Invariant Check
notes: Slow down here because this check prevents mysticism. The coboundary does not square to zero by a new geometric coincidence. It squares to zero because boundary squared zero survives dualization. In a matrix model, students can literally transpose the boundary matrices and see the same zero product appear in the reversed direction.

title: Universal Coefficients
notes: Present the exact sequence as a sorting device. The Hom term is the part students expect after hearing duality, while Ext is the part that stops the story from being only linear algebra. The sequence also models a recurring habit in the chapter: cohomology is dual, but coefficients decide which dual information is visible.

title: Kunneth Product Grid
notes: Use the grid as a degree organizer before mentioning any algebraic caveat. Students should first see that a class from degree p and a class from degree q naturally contributes to degree p plus q on the product. Then add the caution: the tensor grid is clean over favorable coefficients, while Tor terms record the torsion that the grid alone would hide.

title: Why The Diagonal Matters
notes: Make the diagonal feel inevitable rather than technical. Homology classes naturally form external products on a product space, but to multiply them back on X one would need a multiplication on X itself. Cohomology reverses direction, so the universal diagonal map is enough. This is the first real payoff of contravariance.

title: Cup Product On A Simplex
notes: Read the formula geometrically. The simplex is not duplicated; it is split into a front face and a back face with an overlapping vertex. One cochain evaluates the front part, the other evaluates the back part, and the values multiply. This makes degree addition concrete before the ring language arrives.

title: Cup Degree Lab
notes: Let the embedded lab do the motion, but name what students should inspect. The important invariant is degree addition: the product of a degree k class and a degree ell class lands in degree k plus ell. The unit in degree zero should be heard as the cohomological analogue of the constant function one.

title: Graded Commutativity
notes: Treat the sign as a geometric bookkeeping cost. Swapping a degree k object past a degree ell object produces k times ell elementary crossings, and each crossing contributes a minus sign. This is why the ring language must always carry degrees. It also explains why mod two examples can look deceptively commutative.

title: Projective Rings
notes: Use projective spaces as the first payoff for ring structure. The additive groups tell us where classes exist, but the truncated polynomial description tells us how one generator powers through the space until dimension cuts it off. The three examples also show that coefficient choice and generator degree are part of the answer.

title: Cup Products Detect Spaces
notes: This comparison is the conceptual center of the lecture. If students remember only additive groups, the wedge of a two-sphere and a four-sphere can look too similar to the complex projective plane. The cup square separates them. Cohomology rings therefore see attachment and intersection data that group ranks alone erase.

title: Poincare Duality Map
notes: Frame duality as the moment algebra touches manifold geometry. A cohomology class evaluates, but after capping with the fundamental class it also corresponds to a complementary-dimensional homology class. Stress the hypotheses: closedness and orientability are not decorative, because the fundamental class is what makes the global pairing possible.

title: Intersection Is Evaluation
notes: Use this slide to translate the formula into a geometric sentence. First multiply complementary cohomology classes, then evaluate the top-degree result on the fundamental class. On an oriented surface, that number can be read as a signed intersection count. The torus check gives one concrete anchor for the abstraction.

title: Proof Roadmap For Duality
notes: Do not try to prove Poincare duality line by line in one slide. Instead, show the dependency architecture. The proof begins with local orientation, uses compactly supported cohomology to handle pieces, and relies on Mayer-Vietoris to glue. The closed case is then the clean statement students usually quote.

title: Beyond Rings: H-Spaces And SO(n)
notes: This is deliberately a compression slide. The chapter gestures toward H-spaces, classical groups, limits, and Ext, but the companion notebook does not prove full computations for them. The useful message is structural: when a space carries multiplication, cohomology receives a compatible comultiplication, and coefficient-sensitive algebra becomes unavoidable.

title: Bockstein Ladder
notes: Introduce Bockstein as a measurement of failed lifting. A class with coefficients in C may or may not come from B, and the connecting map records the obstruction one degree higher with coefficients in A. This continues the chapter's theme: coefficients are not bookkeeping after the topology is done; they create operations.

title: Transfer Across A Cover
notes: Connect transfer to the intuition of lifting every point to its fiber. The operation sums data over the sheets of a finite cover and keeps track of how many sheets were involved; normalized averaging is a later choice when division by the degree makes sense. The identity p push transfer equals degree times the identity is the key invariant; the local check specializes it to degree two.

title: Local Coefficients And Monodromy
notes: Use the lab to make twisting visible. With ordinary coefficients, a coefficient returns unchanged after moving around a loop. With a local system, the loop can act nontrivially, for example by a sign flip. The recorded values, minus one after one loop and one after two loops, give a compact model of monodromy.

title: Chapter Synthesis
notes: Close by returning to the opening thesis. Cohomology is dual to homology, but the reversed-arrow viewpoint makes new structures natural: products from the diagonal, duality from fundamental classes, coefficient operations from exact sequences, and monodromy from twisted transport. The check badges give students a concrete list of invariants the chapter artifacts verify.
